LABYRINTH

You Were Expected.

Beneath an abandoned ceremonial road lies a labyrinth erased from maps, memories, and history itself.

ENTER THE LABYRINTH

Created by: Adrian Blackshire and Claude

Descend Into The Dark

Far beneath the earth, living roots twist through forgotten halls, sealed crypts, and ruined shrines. Ancient stone corridors pulse with unnatural growth. Every path stretches deeper than it should.

Travellers have vanished here for centuries. Explorers, thieves, pilgrims, scholars. None returned unchanged.

Tonight, you follow them.

The Labyrinth Is Alive

It Watches

Every corridor shifts. Every shadow lingers too long. Something notices each step you take.

It Remembers

The roots carry echoes of everyone who entered before you. Some whispers are warnings. Others are traps.

It Hungers

The deeper you descend, the harder it becomes to remember why you came.

Features

Explore

Navigate a living labyrinth filled with hidden chambers, druidic relics, and forgotten horrors.

Choose

Every decision alters the journey. Trust, fear, courage, and desperation shape your fate.

Roll

Face dangerous encounters using dice-based skill checks, combat, and survival mechanics.

Survive

Ancient guardians, root-born horrors, and things far older than humanity wait below.

“The first sound you'll hear is your own heartbeat. The second belongs to something else.”

The Warning

Every story begins the same way.

A traveller reaches the gate.

A voice whispers:

Turn Back.

Nobody ever listens.

Before You Go Down

Created by: Adrian Blackshire and Claude

Far below an old ceremonial road lies a labyrinth grown from living roots, carved with druidic runes and guarded long ago by a warden named Vaelric. Travelers say nothing that goes down there comes back up. You are a lone adventurer with a pack, a belt knife and a flint, and you are going down anyway.

  • Read each scene, then pick what you do next.
  • When a check comes up, click to roll the d20. Your bonus is added, and you need to meet or beat the number shown.
  • Your character sheet tracks your HP, armor class, gold and everything you find. Your progress is saved in this browser, and you can keep up to three runs in separate save slots. Use Saves in your items to switch.
  • Your journal keeps a record of each journey in this browser: time played, deaths, gold, items, bounties and treasure. Open it from your items, and you'll get a summary at the end of every chapter. When you come back to a save, a short recap of the story so far reminds you where you left off.
  • The Map button beside your journal opens a hand-drawn map of the realm. The fog lifts off each region as you reach it, and a red mark shows where you are.
  • In a fight, your foe's health shows on the sheet. Land hits in a row to build a combo: +1 to hit for each, +2 damage on the second, and the third is a Rootbreaker that doubles your damage dice. A miss breaks the chain.
  • You name your adventurer when you begin, and the people you meet will use it. You won't walk alone for long: friends join your company, and their bond grows with every third fight you win together and with an evening at camp at the end of each chapter. At the start of most chapters you can hire one sellsword for that chapter, and one who serves you long enough will swear to you and stop charging. Your company softens up foes and catches blows, but the killing blow is always yours.
  • Once you have Vaelric's axe, a travelling armourer at the start of each chapter sells other main-hand weapons: a spear, a maul, a rapier and a burning sword, each swinging differently. Swap between them any time with the Wield button in your Bag. The axe stays on your back, and it keeps you alive whatever you're holding.
  • Won fights can drop weapons in five qualities: Ashen, Tempered, Rootbound, Gloaming and Heartfire (0.34%, a little likelier with every fight that doesn't drop one). Better ones carry traits and once-a-fight actives you fire with quick hands. A bow's active is Onslaught: three arrows at once, each finding its own target. Four weapons ride ready on your harness (five at level 20, six at 40): in a fight, Swap weapon to one is free once a turn, a second swap gives the foe advantage, and pulling one from your pack costs your next swing. You can carry six found weapons; past that, the worst is sold. At level 40, Hobb Tallis or Mattie Gorse will sell you the Warden's Weapon Chest for 1,000 gold: six more places, shared by all your save slots, and safe through any death.
  • Sound is off to start. Turn it on here or from your items for a quiet bed of sound in each region, and the Hesk songs sung out loud.
  • Once a fight, when a blow leaves you at 23% of your HP or less, you can dig in: stop the sweeping marker on the root to heal and harden your guard. You have 3 footholds to dig in with, and one comes back each new chapter. On the road you'll meet creatures of the realm, each with its own trick. Your journal keeps a bestiary of every one you've met, and filling it earns marks that help you on the road in every journey after.

The Proving Ground

Hero against hero on the battle maps. Each turn is 2 steps and one action: strike, sling, shove, or hide your one set of caltrops. End a turn in low cover without acting to brace. At 0 HP a hero yields, and nobody loses gold, gear or a level.
